title: Model footprint sculpting for long-dialogue Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants
creator: Jordan Lee
description:
Background: As we onboard long-dialogue workloads (multi-turn chats and conversation transcripts > 32k tokens) for customers, the combination of continuous batching and KV residency strategy directly impacts both tail latency and GPU residency. This ticket scopes a model-specific memory profiling and footprint-sculpting effort targeted at Llama, Mistral, and Qwen family variants with long-context configurations. The goal is to produce per-variant profile knobs that reduce peak memory by 10-25% on 80GB-class GPUs while maintaining <5% regression in sample quality and keeping 99th percentile latency within SLOs.

What success looks like: documented memory profile artifacts per variant, validated through microbenchmarks and customer-scale replay tests, a minimal set of runtime flags and heuristics (no codegen-level model surgery), and a rollout path for Dedicated and Hosted tiers.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Each targeted variant (Llama-2-70B-long, Mistral-7B-long, Qwen-14B-long) has a memory profile that is checked in to the profile registry.
2) End-to-end synthetic replay (batch mix from production trace) fits within 80GB GPU for configured batch target with <=5% quality delta vs baseline.
3) Benchmarks showing peak memory reduction and maintained latency SLOs are attached.
4) Runtime config documented and feature-flag gated for canary rollout.
5) PRs merged and smoke-tested on dedicated QA cluster.
design_notes:
Approach summary: generate per-variant slice profiles capturing KV size, attention cache layout, and working-set locality for typical long-dialogue token distributions. Use a two-stage calibration: offline profiling with microtraces to derive candidate slice sizes, then live replay with continuous batching toggles to observe residency and spill behavior. Key heuristics to tune: KV slice granularity, prefetch window for KV caching, dynamic eviction thresholds based on batch occupancy, and quantization-aware padding to maintain consistent kernel shapes.

Trade-offs considered: aggressive slicing reduces peak but increases per-token compute overhead and potential fragmentation; larger slices simplify kernel efficiency but risk OOM during batch spikes. We favor hybrid profiles where slice granularity adapts with sequence-length percentiles (e.g., shorter prefixes keep coarse slices).

Hardware assumptions: primary targets A100-80GB and H100-80GB; fallback telemetry captured for L40 and V100 where used in Dedicated customer fleets.
experiment_plan:
1) Offline profiler: run 1000 synthetic traces per variant covering sequence percentiles (p50,p75,p90,p99) capturing KV footprint, allocator internals, and kernel occupancy.
2) Candidate generation: automatic sweep over slice_size ∈ {256,512,1024}, prefetch_window ∈ {1,2,4}, eviction_threshold ∈ {0.6,0.7,0.8}.
3) Microbench: measure peak GPU memory, per-token latency, and throughput for each candidate on a single GPU with controlled continuous batch arrival model.
4) Replay tests: run 24h production trace replay on dedicated QA cluster at scaled load to verify tail behavior.
5) Quality evals: run a curated eval set (Evals repo) to detect generation regressions; threshold for acceptance is <5% metric delta.

Metrics collected: peak_gpu_mem_bytes, p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens_per_second, kv_eviction_count, alloc_fragmentation_ratio, generation_score_delta.
benchmark_results: Initial microbench (draft): Llama-2-70B-long with slice_size=512, prefetch=2 yielded -18% peak memory and +4% per-token latency vs baseline; Mistral-7B-long saw -12% memory and +1% latency; Qwen-14B-long saw -22% memory and +6% latency. Fragmentation reduced from 0.27 to 0.19 in best candidate. These runs were on A100-80GB with synthetic steady arrival. Full replay pending. (raw logs: https://storage.redwood.ai/benchmarks/ENG-944400/initial.zip)
rollout_plan:
1) Check in profiles to profile-registry with feature-flag enabled (ff_runtime_model_profiles).
2) Canary on Hosted region us-west-2 with 5% traffic using new profiles and continuous batching config.
3) Monitor costs, SLOs, and quality via console dashboards for 48 hours.
4) If stable, expand to Dedicated QA fleets, then to all Hosted on 2-week cadence.
5) Provide migration notes and toggle to revert to baseline quickly if regressions observed.
risks:
- Quality regressions from slice alignment and quantization interactions.
- Unexpected allocator fragmentation for adversarial long dialogues causing OOMs.
- Increased per-token latency impacting latency-sensitive customers.
- Edge cases on on-prem GPUs with different allocator behavior.
Mitigations: run aggressive eval gating, emergency revert feature-flag, conservative default profiles for Dedicated customers, and pre-deploy simulation for customer's fleet configuration.
